ramayana-3-34-20.translation: Then afterwards I will strike Rama easily, wasted by the loss of his wife, with a confident heart, my purpose fulfilled.'
ramayana-3-34-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-21.translation: Hearing talk of Rama, the great Maricha's mouth went dry and he was terrified.
ramayana-3-34-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-34-22.translation: His heart frightened and dejected, knowing Rama's valour in the great forest, Maricha with joined palms spoke the truth to Ravana, good for him and good for himself.
ramayana-3-34-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 34: Ravana tells Maricha of Khara's defeat and asks him to become a golden deer to lure Rama away so that Ravana can seize Sita.

ramayana-3-35-1.translation: Hearing the lord of demons' words, wise Maricha, skilled in speech, replied to the lord of demons:
ramayana-3-35-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-2.translation: 'People who always speak pleasantly are easy to find, king; but one who speaks unpleasant but beneficial truth, and one who listens to it, are rare.
ramayana-3-35-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka. A widely quoted line on honest counsel.

ramayana-3-35-3.translation: Surely you do not understand Rama, mighty and great in virtue, like great Indra and Varuna, since you have no spies and are fickle.
ramayana-3-35-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-4.translation: Will there be well-being for all demons on earth, dear one? Will Rama, enraged, not rid the world of demons?
ramayana-3-35-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-5.translation: Was Janaka's daughter not born to end your life? Will Sita not become the cause of great disaster?
ramayana-3-35-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-6.translation: Having you as lord, desire-driven and unrestrained, will Lanka not be destroyed with you and its demons?
ramayana-3-35-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-7.translation: For a king like you, driven by desire, of bad character and evil counsel, the foolish king destroys himself, his people and his kingdom.
ramayana-3-35-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-8.translation: He was not cast out by his father, he has never gone beyond bounds, he is not greedy, nor ill-natured, nor a disgrace to warriors.
ramayana-3-35-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-9.translation: Kausalya's son is not lacking in the virtues of dharma; nor is he harsh, but devoted to the good of all beings.
ramayana-3-35-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-10.translation: Seeing his truthful father deceived by Kaikeyi, the righteous one said 'I will do it' and went to the forest.
ramayana-3-35-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-11.translation: To please Kaikeyi and his father Dasharatha, he gave up the kingdom and pleasures and entered the Dandaka forest.
ramayana-3-35-11.meaning: He gave up all for duty.
ramayana-3-35-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-12.translation: Rama is not harsh, dear one, nor ignorant, nor uncontrolled. You must not speak such untruths that are not even heard of.
ramayana-3-35-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-13.translation: Rama is dharma in bodily form, a good man of true valour, king of the whole world, as Indra is of the gods.
ramayana-3-35-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka. One of the most famous descriptions of Rama, spoken by his enemy.

ramayana-3-35-14.translation: How can you wish to carry off by force Sita, protected by his own power, like the light of the sun?
ramayana-3-35-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-15.translation: You should not suddenly enter the blazing fire of Rama, unassailable in battle, whose flames are arrows and whose fuel is bow and sword.
ramayana-3-35-15.meaning: Do not walk into this fire.
ramayana-3-35-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-16.translation: With his bow like a gaping blazing mouth, his arrows like flames, intolerant, the hero holding bow and arrows, destroyer of enemy armies,
ramayana-3-35-16.meaning: He is Death to his foes.
ramayana-3-35-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-17.translation: you should not approach Rama, like Death, giving up kingdom, happiness and your own dear life, dear one.
ramayana-3-35-17.meaning: Do not throw away your life.
ramayana-3-35-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-18.translation: Immeasurable is the power of him whose wife is Janaka's daughter; you cannot carry her off in the forest, sheltered by Rama's bow.
ramayana-3-35-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-19.translation: Dearer to him than life, always devoted, slender-waisted Sita is like the flame of a blazing fire.
ramayana-3-35-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-20.translation: What use is this pointless effort, lord of demons? If he sees you in battle, that is the end of your life, and of your happiness and your kingdom, so hard to win.
ramayana-3-35-20.meaning: This plan will cost you everything.
ramayana-3-35-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-21.translation: Consult with all your ministers, led by the righteous Vibhishana, and then make up your own mind.
ramayana-3-35-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-35-22.translation: Weigh the strength of the faults and merits, know truly your own strength and Rama's, decide what is good for you, and then do what is fitting.
ramayana-3-35-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka. Sound advice on deliberation.

ramayana-3-35-23.translation: I think a battle with the son of the king of Kosala is not right for you. Listen further to my words, which are best, fitting and proper, lord of night-roamers.
ramayana-3-35-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 35: Maricha bravely warns Ravana that Rama is righteousness in human form and that seizing Sita will destroy Lanka.

ramayana-3-36-1.translation: Once, proud of my strength, I roamed this earth, mountain-like, with the strength of a thousand elephants,
ramayana-3-36-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-2.translation: dark as a blue cloud, with earrings of refined gold, frightening the world, crowned and armed with an iron club, roaming the Dandaka forest eating the flesh of sages.
ramayana-3-36-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-3.translation: Then the righteous great sage Vishvamitra, frightened of me, went himself to King Dasharatha and said:
ramayana-3-36-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-4.translation: 'Let Rama guard me attentively at the time of the holy rite; a terrible fear has arisen for me from Maricha, lord of men.'
ramayana-3-36-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-5.translation: Thus addressed, the righteous King Dasharatha replied to the noble great sage Vishvamitra:
ramayana-3-36-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-6.translation: 'Rama is not yet sixteen and untrained in weapons. My whole army will go with me if you wish; I will kill your enemy as you desire, best of sages.'
ramayana-3-36-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-7.translation: Thus addressed, the sage said to the king again: 'No strength in the world but Rama's is enough for that demon.
ramayana-3-36-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-8.translation: Though a boy, this mighty one can subdue him. I will go, taking Rama; may all be well with you, scorcher of foes.'
ramayana-3-36-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-9.translation: Having said this, the sage Vishvamitra, very pleased, took the prince and went to his own hermitage.
ramayana-3-36-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-10.translation: Then in the Dandaka forest Rama stood guard over the one consecrated for the sacrifice, twanging his bright bow.
ramayana-3-36-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-11.translation: Beardless yet, glorious, a dark boy with lovely eyes, wearing a single cloth, bow in hand, with a topknot and a golden garland,
ramayana-3-36-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-12.translation: lighting up the Dandaka forest with his own blazing power, Rama looked like the young moon risen.
ramayana-3-36-12.meaning: He shone like the new moon.
ramayana-3-36-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-13.translation: Then I, like a cloud, with earrings of refined gold, strong and proud of my boon, came to that hermitage.
ramayana-3-36-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-14.translation: He saw me enter suddenly with weapon raised; seeing me, he calmly strung his bow.
ramayana-3-36-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-15.translation: Despising Rama in my delusion, thinking 'He is a boy', I rushed in haste at Vishvamitra's altar.
ramayana-3-36-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-16.translation: Then he released a sharp, foe-destroying arrow; struck by it, I was flung a hundred yojanas into the sea.
ramayana-3-36-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-17.translation: Thrown off by the force of Rama's arrow, my senses reeling, I was cast into the deep waters of the ocean; regaining consciousness after a long time, I went to the city of Lanka.
ramayana-3-36-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-18.translation: So I was spared then, but my companions were killed by Rama, a boy untrained in weapons, tireless in his deeds.
ramayana-3-36-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-19.translation: So if, though I warn you, you make war on Rama, you will soon meet terrible disaster and perish.
ramayana-3-36-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-20.translation: You will bring suffering and ruin on the demons, who know play and love and delight in gatherings and festivals.
ramayana-3-36-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-21.translation: You will see the city of Lanka, crowded with mansions and palaces and adorned with many jewels, destroyed for the sake of Sita.
ramayana-3-36-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-22.translation: Even the pure who do no evil perish through the sins of others because they shelter with the wicked, as fish in a serpent's pool.
ramayana-3-36-22.meaning: The innocent suffer for the leader's sins.
ramayana-3-36-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again. A teaching on how one person's wrongdoing harms many.

ramayana-3-36-23.translation: You will see demons, their limbs anointed with divine sandal and adorned with divine ornaments, struck down on the ground through your fault.
ramayana-3-36-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-24.translation: You will see night-roamers, with wives seized or still with them, the survivors, fleeing in ten directions without refuge.
ramayana-3-36-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-25.translation: You will surely see Lanka covered with a net of arrows, wrapped in flames, its houses burned.
ramayana-3-36-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-26.translation: You have thousands of women, king; be devoted to your own wives and save your own clan, demon.
ramayana-3-36-26.meaning: Be content with what you have.
ramayana-3-36-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-27.translation: If you wish to enjoy honour, prosperity, kingdom and your own dear life for long, do nothing to displease Rama.
ramayana-3-36-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-36-28.translation: If, though strongly restrained by me, your friend, you seize Sita by force, you will go to Yama's realm with your strength spent and your kin, your life taken by Rama's arrows.'
ramayana-3-36-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 36: Maricha tells how the boy Rama, guarding Vishvamitra's sacrifice, flung him a hundred yojanas into the sea, and warns Ravana again.

ramayana-3-37-1.translation: 'So I escaped then from him in battle somehow. Now hear what happened afterwards.
ramayana-3-37-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-2.translation: Still not humbled, I entered the Dandaka forest with two demons, all of us in the form of deer.
ramayana-3-37-2.meaning: He went back in deer form.
ramayana-3-37-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-3.translation: With blazing tongue, huge body, sharp horns and great strength, I roamed the Dandaka forest as a great flesh-eating beast.
ramayana-3-37-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-4.translation: At fire offerings, bathing places and sacred trees, I roamed very fiercely, Ravana, attacking those ascetics.
ramayana-3-37-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-5.translation: Killing the ascetics who followed dharma in the Dandaka forest, I drank their blood and ate their flesh.
ramayana-3-37-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-6.translation: Eating the flesh of sages, cruel, terrifying the forest-dwellers, drunk with blood, I roamed the Dandaka forest.
ramayana-3-37-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-7.translation: Then, roaming the Dandaka forest as a corrupter of dharma, I came upon Rama, an ascetic devoted to dharma,
ramayana-3-37-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-8.translation: with the noble Sita and the great warrior Lakshmana, an ascetic restrained in diet, devoted to the good of all beings.
ramayana-3-37-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-9.translation: Despising mighty Rama living in the forest, thinking 'He is an ascetic', and remembering the old enmity,
ramayana-3-37-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-10.translation: I rushed at him in fury in deer form with sharp horns, wanting to kill him, foolishly, remembering that blow.
ramayana-3-37-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-11.translation: He released three sharp, foe-destroying arrows, drawing his strong bow, swift as Garuda or the wind.
ramayana-3-37-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-12.translation: Those three very dreadful, blood-drinking, smooth-jointed arrows, like thunderbolts, came together.
ramayana-3-37-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-13.translation: Knowing Rama's valour and having seen the danger before, I cunningly leapt away and escaped; the other two demons were killed.
ramayana-3-37-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-14.translation: Freed somehow from Rama's arrow, keeping my life, I have renounced the world here and become an ascetic, disciplined and composed.
ramayana-3-37-14.meaning: He became a hermit out of fear.
ramayana-3-37-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-15.translation: In every tree I see Rama, wearing bark and black deerskin, bow in hand, like Death with a noose in his hand.
ramayana-3-37-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-16.translation: In fear I see thousands of Ramas, Ravana; this whole forest seems to me to be made of Rama.
ramayana-3-37-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear. Fear has made Maricha think of Rama constantly; tradition notes the irony that this constant remembrance is a kind of devotion.

ramayana-3-37-17.translation: I see Rama even when alone, lord of demons; seeing Rama in my dreams, I wake up distraught.
ramayana-3-37-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-18.translation: For me, terrified of Rama, Ravana, names that begin with 'ra', even ratna (jewel) and ratha (chariot), cause fear.
ramayana-3-37-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-19.translation: I know his power; a battle with him is not right for you. Fight Rama in battle or forgive him, demon; but do not speak of Rama to me if you want to see me.
ramayana-3-37-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-37-20.translation: If you do not accept these words spoken by me, who wishes my kin well, you will lose your life in battle today with your kin, killed by Rama with straight arrows.'
ramayana-3-37-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 37: Maricha tells how he attacked Rama again in deer form and barely escaped; now he sees Rama everywhere in fear.

ramayana-3-38-1.translation: Ravana did not accept Maricha's fitting and proper words, like a man who wants to die refusing medicine.
ramayana-3-38-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer. The image of a dying man refusing medicine is a famous simile for rejecting wise counsel.

ramayana-3-38-2.translation: Driven by fate, the lord of demons spoke harsh, improper words to Maricha, who had spoken what was wholesome and good:
ramayana-3-38-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-3.translation: 'These improper words you speak to me, Maricha, are utterly fruitless, like seed sown in salty ground.
ramayana-3-38-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-4.translation: Your words cannot break my resolve to fight Rama, especially as he is an evil-natured, foolish man,
ramayana-3-38-4.meaning: He would not change his mind.
ramayana-3-38-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-5.translation: who, leaving friends, kingdom, mother and father, went to the forest at a single word from a common woman.
ramayana-3-38-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-6.translation: I must certainly carry off Sita, dearer to him than life, from that killer of Khara, in your presence.
ramayana-3-38-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-7.translation: This resolve is firm in my heart, Maricha; it cannot be turned back even by gods and demons with Indra.
ramayana-3-38-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-8.translation: You should speak of fault or merit only when asked, or of the danger or means in deciding this matter.
ramayana-3-38-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-9.translation: A wise minister who wants his own prosperity should speak to the king only when asked, with joined palms.
ramayana-3-38-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-10.translation: A king should be spoken to with words that do not oppose him, gently, auspiciously, beneficially and with courtesy.
ramayana-3-38-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-11.translation: A king worthy of honour does not welcome words, however beneficial, spoken with contempt and lacking respect.
ramayana-3-38-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-12.translation: Kings of boundless might bear five forms: of Agni, Indra, Soma, Yama and Varuna, namely heat, valour, gentleness, punishment and graciousness.
ramayana-3-38-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-13.translation: So kings are to be honoured and respected in every situation; but you, not knowing dharma, rely only on delusion.
ramayana-3-38-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-14.translation: Out of wickedness you speak harshly to me, your guest. I am not asking about merits and faults, or what is right for me, demon; you must give help in this task.
ramayana-3-38-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-15.translation: Become a golden deer spotted with silver, tempt Sita, and then go where you like.
ramayana-3-38-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-16.translation: Seeing you, a magical golden deer, Sita, filled with wonder, will quickly say to Rama, "Bring it!"
ramayana-3-38-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-17.translation: When Rama and Lakshmana have gone, I will carry off Sita at my ease, as Indra carried off Shachi.
ramayana-3-38-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-18.translation: Having done this, go where you like, demon. I will give you half my kingdom, Maricha of good vows.
ramayana-3-38-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-19.translation: Go on an auspicious path, gentle one, for the success of this work. Having won Sita without a fight, by deceiving Rama, I will go to Lanka with you, my purpose done.
ramayana-3-38-19.meaning: He planned to win by trickery.
ramayana-3-38-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-20.translation: You will do this for me even by force; one who opposes a king never prospers.
ramayana-3-38-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-38-21.translation: Going to him your life is in doubt, but opposing me your death is certain today. Consider this properly and do what is best.'
ramayana-3-38-21.meaning: Choose: risk with Rama or certain death now.
ramayana-3-38-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 38: Ravana rejects Maricha's advice, lectures him on how to speak to a king, and orders him to become the golden deer.

ramayana-3-39-1.translation: Ordered like a king with hostile words, the night-roamer Maricha spoke harshly to the lord of demons:
ramayana-3-39-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-2.translation: 'What evil-doer has advised you to this ruin, of yourself, your sons, your kingdom and your ministers, night-roamer?
ramayana-3-39-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-3.translation: What sinner does not rejoice in your happiness, king? Who has cleverly shown you this door to death?
ramayana-3-39-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-4.translation: Clearly your enemies, weak in strength, wish to see you perish, caught by one stronger.
ramayana-3-39-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-5.translation: What mean, ill-speaking person has advised you so, wishing you to perish by your own deed, night-roamer?
ramayana-3-39-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-6.translation: Surely your ministers deserve death and are not being killed, Ravana, since they do not restrain you at all when you have taken the wrong road.
ramayana-3-39-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-7.translation: A king driven by desire who has taken a wrong path must always be restrained by good ministers; you who should be restrained are not.
ramayana-3-39-7.meaning: Good advisers must check a wayward ruler.
ramayana-3-39-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-8.translation: By their master's favour, ministers gain dharma, wealth, pleasure and fame, best of victors.
ramayana-3-39-8.meaning: Ministers depend on a good ruler.
ramayana-3-39-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-9.translation: But when it is otherwise, all that is in vain, Ravana; other people meet disaster through their master's faults.
ramayana-3-39-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-10.translation: For dharma and victory are rooted in the king, best of victors; so the king must be protected in every situation.
ramayana-3-39-10.meaning: The ruler is the root of his people's good.
ramayana-3-39-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-11.translation: A kingdom cannot be protected by one who is harsh, night-roamer, nor by one who is perverse or undisciplined.
ramayana-3-39-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-12.translation: Ministers who give harsh counsel are broken along with the king, like chariots with poor drivers on rough ground.
ramayana-3-39-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-13.translation: Many good people in the world who practise dharma properly have perished with their families through the fault of others.
ramayana-3-39-13.meaning: The good suffer for others' faults.
ramayana-3-39-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-14.translation: Subjects protected by a harsh, perverse master do not prosper, Ravana, any more than sheep guarded by a jackal.
ramayana-3-39-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-15.translation: All the demons will surely perish, Ravana, whose king is you, harsh, foolish and without self-control.
ramayana-3-39-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-16.translation: This terrible disaster has come on you by chance, like the crow and the palm fruit; what good is it that you will perish with your army?
ramayana-3-39-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana and his ministers, warning that a harsh king destroys his whole people.

ramayana-3-39-17.translation: Having killed me, Rama will soon kill you. By this I have done my part: I will die killed by an enemy.
ramayana-3-39-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana, warning that seizing Sita will destroy them all.

ramayana-3-39-18.translation: Consider me dead at the very sight of Rama, and know yourself dead with your kin once you carry off Sita.
ramayana-3-39-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana, warning that seizing Sita will destroy them all.

ramayana-3-39-19.translation: If you bring Sita from the hermitage with me, neither you nor I nor Lanka nor the demons will survive.
ramayana-3-39-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana, warning that seizing Sita will destroy them all.

ramayana-3-39-20.translation: Though warned by me, who wish you well, you will not bear these words, night-roamer; for men whose life is over, as good as dead, do not accept the good advice of friends.'
ramayana-3-39-20.meaning: Those set on ruin ignore counsel.
ramayana-3-39-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 39: Maricha rebukes Ravana, warning that seizing Sita will destroy them all.

ramayana-3-40-1.translation: Having spoken so harshly to Ravana, Maricha, wretched and afraid of the lord of night-roamers, said, 'Let us go.'
ramayana-3-40-1.meaning: Maricha gave in out of fear.
ramayana-3-40-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-2.translation: 'Once he sees me again, with bow, arrows and sword, weapon raised to kill me, my life is gone.
ramayana-3-40-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-3.translation: But what can I do with you being so wicked? Here I go, dear one; may you fare well, night-roamer.'
ramayana-3-40-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-4.translation: The demon was delighted by those words, embraced him tightly and said:
ramayana-3-40-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-5.translation: 'These are brave words, as if spoken by my own wish. Now you are Maricha; before, you were some other night-roamer.
ramayana-3-40-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-6.translation: Quickly mount this jewelled, sky-going chariot with me, yoked to goblin-faced donkeys.'
ramayana-3-40-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-7.translation: Then Ravana and Maricha mounted that chariot like a celestial car and quickly left that circle of hermitages.
ramayana-3-40-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-8.translation: Looking at towns, forests, mountains, all rivers, kingdoms and cities as they went,
ramayana-3-40-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-9.translation: reaching the Dandaka forest, Ravana, lord of demons, with Maricha saw Rama's hermitage.
ramayana-3-40-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-10.translation: Getting down from that gold-adorned chariot, Ravana took Maricha by the hand and said:
ramayana-3-40-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-11.translation: 'There is Rama's hermitage, surrounded by plantains. Do quickly, friend, what we came for.'
ramayana-3-40-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-12.translation: Hearing Ravana's words, the demon Maricha became a deer and wandered by the door of Rama's hermitage.
ramayana-3-40-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-13.translation: The tips of his horns were the finest gems, his face white and dark, his mouth like a red lotus, his ears like blue sapphire lotuses,
ramayana-3-40-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-14.translation: his neck slightly raised, his belly like sapphire, his flanks like madhuka flowers, the colour of lotus filaments,
ramayana-3-40-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-15.translation: hooves like beryl, slender legs, well-knit, shining with its tail raised up, coloured like the rainbow,
ramayana-3-40-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-16.translation: of lovely glossy colour, covered with many kinds of jewels: in a moment the demon became a most beautiful deer.
ramayana-3-40-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-17.translation: Lighting up the lovely forest and Rama's hermitage, the demon took on a charming, beautiful form.
ramayana-3-40-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-18.translation: To tempt Sita, coloured with many minerals, he wandered gracefully over the grassy places all around.
ramayana-3-40-18.meaning: He played to catch Sita's eye.
ramayana-3-40-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-19.translation: Spotted with hundreds of silver drops and lovely to see, he wandered about breaking and eating the young shoots of trees.
ramayana-3-40-19.meaning: He grazed like a real deer.
ramayana-3-40-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-20.translation: Going to the plantain bower and here and there among the karnikara trees, he moved slowly into Sita's sight.
ramayana-3-40-20.meaning: He moved where Sita would see.
ramayana-3-40-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-21.translation: With its back patterned like lotuses, the great deer shone, wandering freely near Rama's hermitage.
ramayana-3-40-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-22.translation: The finest of deer would go away and come back, run off for a moment and quickly return again.
ramayana-3-40-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-23.translation: Playing, it would sit on the ground again; coming to the hermitage door, it would go off to the herds of deer.
ramayana-3-40-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-24.translation: Followed by herds of deer, it would turn back again; the demon in deer form longed to be seen by Sita.
ramayana-3-40-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-25.translation: It wandered, leaping in lovely circles. All the other forest deer looked at it,
ramayana-3-40-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-26.translation: came near, sniffed it, and fled in ten directions. The demon, though given to killing deer, did not eat those wild deer,
ramayana-3-40-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-27.translation: touching them but not eating, to hide his true nature. At that very time lovely-eyed Sita
ramayana-3-40-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-28.translation: was busy gathering flowers among the trees. The bright-eyed one passed karnikara, ashoka and mango trees
ramayana-3-40-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-29.translation: picking flowers, lovely-faced. That noble lady, who did not deserve forest life, saw the jewelled deer, its body patterned with pearls and gems.
ramayana-3-40-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-30.translation: With lovely teeth and lips, its hair like silver, she gazed at it fondly, her eyes wide with wonder.
ramayana-3-40-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-31.translation: And the magical deer, looking at Rama's beloved, wandered there as if setting the forest alight.
ramayana-3-40-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-40-32.translation: Seeing that deer made of many jewels, such as she had never seen before, Sita, daughter of Janaka, was filled with great wonder.
ramayana-3-40-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 40: Maricha agrees out of fear, flies with Ravana to Panchavati and turns into a dazzling jewelled deer, which Sita sees.

ramayana-3-41-1.translation: Gathering flowers, the lovely one looked at it, adorned with flanks of gold and silver.
ramayana-3-41-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-2.translation: Delighted, the flawless one, bright as polished gold, called out to her husband and to Lakshmana with his weapons.
ramayana-3-41-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-3.translation: Called by Sita, Rama and Lakshmana, tigers among men, looked around the place and saw the deer.
ramayana-3-41-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-4.translation: Seeing it, Lakshmana was suspicious and said to Rama: 'I think this deer is the demon Maricha himself.
ramayana-3-41-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-5.translation: Kings happily hunting in the forest have been killed by this wicked shape-shifter through just such a disguise, Rama.
ramayana-3-41-5.meaning: Maricha has killed hunters this way.
ramayana-3-41-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-6.translation: This magical deer form has been made by this master of illusion, tiger among men, shining like a mirage city of the gandharvas.
ramayana-3-41-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-7.translation: No such jewel-patterned deer exists in the world, Rama, lord of the world; this is illusion, no doubt.'
ramayana-3-41-7.meaning: No real deer looks like that.
ramayana-3-41-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-8.translation: As he spoke, bright-smiling Sita, her mind captured by the deception, stopped him and said joyfully:
ramayana-3-41-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-9.translation: 'My noble husband, this lovely deer steals my heart. Bring it, mighty-armed one; it will be our plaything.
ramayana-3-41-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-10.translation: Many holy-looking deer roam together here at our hermitage, yaks and srimaras,
ramayana-3-41-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-11.translation: bears, herds of spotted deer, monkeys and kinnaras roam, mighty-armed one, finest in form and very strong,
ramayana-3-41-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-12.translation: but never before, king, have I seen a deer like this best of deer, in radiance, gentleness and brilliance.
ramayana-3-41-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-13.translation: Its body patterned with many colours, studded with drops of jewels, lighting up the forest calmly, it shines like the moon.
ramayana-3-41-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-14.translation: Ah, what form, what beauty, and what lovely voice! This wonderful, colourful deer seems to steal my heart.
ramayana-3-41-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-15.translation: If the deer can be caught alive by you, it will be a marvel and will cause wonder.
ramayana-3-41-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-16.translation: When our forest life is over and we are back in the kingdom, this deer will adorn the inner palace.
ramayana-3-41-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-17.translation: This divine deer will cause wonder for Bharata, for you, for my mothers-in-law and for me, lord.
ramayana-3-41-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-18.translation: If this finest of deer cannot be caught alive, its skin will be lovely for me, tiger among men.
ramayana-3-41-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-19.translation: I would like to sit on its golden skin spread on a bed of grass when the creature is killed.
ramayana-3-41-19.meaning: She wished to sit on it.
ramayana-3-41-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-20.translation: This wilful wish is harsh and thought unbecoming for women; but this creature's body has filled me with wonder.'
ramayana-3-41-20.meaning: She knew the wish was not quite right.
ramayana-3-41-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita. Sita herself admits the wish is a whim; the moment shows how desire can cloud judgment.

ramayana-3-41-21.translation: By that deer with golden hair, horns of the finest gems, the colour of the young sun and the brilliance of the starry path, even Rama's mind was filled with wonder.
ramayana-3-41-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-22.translation: Hearing Sita's words and seeing the wonderful deer, Rama, delighted, said to his brother Lakshmana:
ramayana-3-41-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-23.translation: 'See, Lakshmana, Sita's longing for this deer. Because of its surpassing beauty this deer will not live today.
ramayana-3-41-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-24.translation: Not in the Nandana grove nor in Chaitraratha, much less on earth, Lakshmana, is there any deer equal to this one.
ramayana-3-41-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-25.translation: Its lovely rows of hair, lying against and with the grain, shine on the deer, patterned with drops of gold.
ramayana-3-41-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-26.translation: See, as it yawns, its blazing tongue like a flame comes out of its mouth, like lightning from a cloud.
ramayana-3-41-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-27.translation: Its mouth of emerald and crystal, its belly like conch and pearl, whose mind would this indescribable deer not tempt?
ramayana-3-41-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-28.translation: Whose mind would not be filled with wonder, seeing this divine form, made of many jewels and shining like gold?
ramayana-3-41-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-29.translation: Kings who are archers kill deer while hunting in the great forest, for meat and for sport, Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-41-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-30.translation: By effort, riches are gathered in the great forest, and many kinds of minerals with gems, jewels and gold.
ramayana-3-41-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-31.translation: All that is the whole essence of men's wealth, increasing their store, like all that Shukra thinks of in his mind, Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-41-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-32.translation: The object for which a seeker goes without hesitation, experts in the science of wealth call that wealth, Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-41-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-33.translation: Slender-waisted Sita will sit with me on the precious golden skin of this jewel among deer.
ramayana-3-41-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-34.translation: Neither kadali, priyaki, praveni nor aviki hide would equal it in softness, I think.
ramayana-3-41-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-35.translation: This splendid deer and the divine one that moves in the sky, both are divine deer: the star-deer and the earth-deer.
ramayana-3-41-35.meaning: It is like the deer in the stars.
ramayana-3-41-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-36.translation: Or if it is as you say, Lakshmana, an illusion of the demon, then I must kill it.
ramayana-3-41-36.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-37.translation: For this cruel Maricha, of unformed soul, roaming the forest before, has harmed the best of sages.
ramayana-3-41-37.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-38.translation: He has risen up and killed many kings, great archers, while they hunted; so this deer must be killed.
ramayana-3-41-38.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-39.translation: Here before, Vatapi, despising ascetics, killed brahmins from inside their bellies, as its own foetus kills a mule.
ramayana-3-41-39.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-40.translation: After a long time he came upon the mighty great sage Agastya in the world and became his food.
ramayana-3-41-40.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-41.translation: Seeing him wanting to resume his form as he rose, the holy one smiled and said to Vatapi:
ramayana-3-41-41.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-42.translation: "Vatapi, because you heedlessly overpowered the best of brahmins in the world with your power, you are now digested."
ramayana-3-41-42.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-43.translation: So, Lakshmana, that demon would not survive, like Vatapi, who despises one like me, always devoted to dharma and master of his senses.
ramayana-3-41-43.meaning: Rama trusts dharma to protect him.
ramayana-3-41-43.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-44.translation: He will be killed, as Vatapi by Agastya. You stay here armed and alert, and guard Sita.
ramayana-3-41-44.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-45.translation: All that we have to do depends on her, Lakshmana. I will kill this deer or catch it.
ramayana-3-41-45.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-46.translation: While I go quickly to bring the deer, Lakshmana, see how Sita longs for its skin.
ramayana-3-41-46.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-47.translation: Because of its superb skin, this deer will not live today. You must stay watchful at the hermitage with Sita
ramayana-3-41-47.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-48.translation: until I kill the spotted deer with a single arrow. Having killed it, I will take the skin and come back quickly, Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-41-48.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-41-49.translation: With the wise, very strong bird Jatayu, Lakshmana, be watchful; take charge of Sita, suspicious every moment on every side.'
ramayana-3-41-49.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 41: Sita asks Rama to catch the golden deer; Lakshmana suspects it is Maricha, but Rama decides to go, leaving Lakshmana to guard Sita.

ramayana-3-42-1.translation: Having instructed his brother thus, mighty Rama, delight of the Raghus, bound on his sword with its gold hilt.
ramayana-3-42-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer deep into the forest.

ramayana-3-42-2.translation: Then, taking his bow, bent in three places, his own ornament, and binding on two quivers, he went with lofty stride.
ramayana-3-42-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer deep into the forest.

ramayana-3-42-3.translation: Seeing the king of kings rushing at him, the deer, deceiving him, vanished in fear and then appeared again.
ramayana-3-42-3.meaning: The deer played hide and seek.
ramayana-3-42-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer deep into the forest.

ramayana-3-42-4.translation: With his sword bound on, he took his bow and ran to where the deer was; he saw it ahead, as if shining with its beauty.
ramayana-3-42-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer deep into the forest.

ramayana-3-42-5.translation: Looking again and again at it running in the great forest, bow in hand, he saw it sometimes beyond arrow's range, tempting him.
ramayana-3-42-5.meaning: It stayed just out of reach.
ramayana-3-42-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer deep into the forest.

ramayana-3-42-6.translation: Wary and darting, as if leaping into the sky, it was seen and then unseen in various new places.
ramayana-3-42-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-7.translation: Like the autumn moon veiled by scattered clouds, it was seen for a moment and then shone again from far off.
ramayana-3-42-7.meaning: It flickered in and out of view.
ramayana-3-42-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-8.translation: By appearing and disappearing it drew Rama away; Rama grew angry, helpless and bewildered by it.
ramayana-3-42-8.meaning: The deer led Rama far away.
ramayana-3-42-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-9.translation: Then it stood still, as if very tired, in the shade on a grassy spot, surrounded by wild deer, seen not far off.
ramayana-3-42-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-10.translation: Seeing it, mighty Rama, resolved to kill it, fitted an arrow to his strong bow and drew it powerfully,
ramayana-3-42-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-11.translation: and aiming at that deer, he released a blazing, bright arrow made with Brahma's weapon, like a flaming serpent.
ramayana-3-42-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-12.translation: That excellent arrow, like a thunderbolt, tore through the deer form and pierced the heart of Maricha himself.
ramayana-3-42-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-13.translation: Leaping up a palm tree's height, struck by the arrow, he fell; nearly dead on the ground he let out a terrible cry, and dying, Maricha gave up that false body.
ramayana-3-42-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-14.translation: Knowing his time had come, he cried out in a voice just like Rama's: 'Ah Sita! Ah Lakshmana!'
ramayana-3-42-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-15.translation: Pierced in a vital spot by that peerless arrow, Maricha left the deer form, took his own huge demon form and gave up his life.
ramayana-3-42-15.meaning: He died in his true form.
ramayana-3-42-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-16.translation: Struck by the arrow, he became a demon with colourful armlets and every ornament, a golden garland and great fangs.
ramayana-3-42-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-17.translation: Seeing the terrible demon fallen on the ground, Rama's mind went to Sita, remembering Lakshmana's words.
ramayana-3-42-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-18.translation: 'This demon died crying out loudly "Ah Sita! Ah Lakshmana!"; how will Sita be when she hears it?
ramayana-3-42-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-19.translation: And what state will mighty-armed Lakshmana be in?' Thinking thus, the righteous Rama's hair stood on end.
ramayana-3-42-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-20.translation: Then a sharp fear born of despair entered Rama, having killed the demon in deer form and heard that cry.
ramayana-3-42-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-42-21.translation: Killing another spotted deer and taking the meat, Rama hurried back toward Janasthana.
ramayana-3-42-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 42: Rama chases the elusive deer and finally shoots it; dying, Maricha cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-43-1.translation: Recognising in the forest the cry of distress like her husband's, Sita said to Lakshmana, 'Go and find out about Rama.
ramayana-3-43-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-2.translation: My life and heart are not steady, for I heard loudly the cry of one in great distress calling out.
ramayana-3-43-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-3.translation: You must save your brother crying out in the forest. Run to him quickly; he is seeking help,
ramayana-3-43-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-4.translation: fallen into the power of demons, like a bull among lions.' Though told this, he did not go, remembering his brother's command.
ramayana-3-43-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-5.translation: Then Janaka's daughter, angry, said to him: 'Lakshmana, in the guise of a friend you are like an enemy to your brother,
ramayana-3-43-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-6.translation: since in this state you do not go to your brother. You want Rama to perish for my sake, Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-43-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes. Sita's fear makes her lash out unfairly; the epic presents it as a moment of panic.

ramayana-3-43-7.translation: I think his misfortune pleases you; you have no love for your brother. That is why you stand here at ease without seeing that radiant one.
ramayana-3-43-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-8.translation: What use is it for me to be here, when he whom you came to serve is in danger?'
ramayana-3-43-8.meaning: Rama matters more than her safety.
ramayana-3-43-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-9.translation: As Sita spoke, flooded with tears and grief, frightened like a doe, Lakshmana said to her:
ramayana-3-43-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-10.translation: 'Queen, among gods and men, gandharvas and birds, demons, pishachas, kinnaras and beasts,
ramayana-3-43-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-11.translation: and terrible danavas, there is none, lovely one, who could fight Rama, equal of Indra, in battle.
ramayana-3-43-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-12.translation: Rama cannot be killed in battle; you should not speak like this. I dare not leave you in this forest without Rama.
ramayana-3-43-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-13.translation: His strength cannot be resisted even by the mightiest, even by the three worlds united with their lords and the gods.
ramayana-3-43-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-14.translation: Let your heart be at peace and give up this anguish; your husband will come back soon having killed that fine deer.
ramayana-3-43-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-15.translation: That was clearly not his voice, nor any god's; it is that demon's illusion, like a mirage city.
ramayana-3-43-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-16.translation: You were entrusted to me as a deposit by great Rama, lovely one; I dare not leave you here.
ramayana-3-43-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-17.translation: And we have made enemies of these night-roamers, gracious one, because of Khara's death and the slaughter at Janasthana.
ramayana-3-43-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-18.translation: Demons in the great forest make many kinds of sounds; they delight in violence. Do not worry about it, Sita.'
ramayana-3-43-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-19.translation: Thus addressed by Lakshmana, angry, her eyes red, she spoke harsh words to truthful Lakshmana:
ramayana-3-43-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-20.translation: 'Ignoble, cruel, merciless, disgrace to your family! I think you speak like this because you want me.
ramayana-3-43-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes. This false accusation is one of the most painful moments in the epic, born of terror for Rama.

ramayana-3-43-21.translation: It is no wonder, Lakshmana, that such evil exists in rivals like you, cruel and always acting in secret.
ramayana-3-43-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-22.translation: Very wicked, you alone have followed Rama alone into the forest, secretly for my sake, or sent by Bharata.
ramayana-3-43-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-23.translation: How could I, having taken refuge with my husband Rama, dark as a blue lotus and lotus-eyed, desire some other man?
ramayana-3-43-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-24.translation: Without doubt I will give up my life before your eyes, Lakshmana; I cannot live a moment on earth without Rama.'
ramayana-3-43-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-25.translation: Thus addressed with harsh, hair-raising words by Sita, Lakshmana, master of his senses, with joined palms, said to Sita:
ramayana-3-43-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-26.translation: 'I dare not answer; you are a deity to me. Unfitting words are not surprising in women, Sita.
ramayana-3-43-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes. Lakshmana's generalisation about women reflects his anger and the attitudes of the time, not a teaching; the epic shows both him and Sita acting under great strain.

ramayana-3-43-27.translation: This is the nature of women seen in the worlds: women abandon dharma, are fickle, sharp and cause division.
ramayana-3-43-27.meaning: Lakshmana speaks in hurt and anger.
ramayana-3-43-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes. Lakshmana's generalisation about women reflects his anger and the attitudes of the time, not a teaching; the epic shows both him and Sita acting under great strain.
