ramayana-3-43-28.translation: Let all the forest-dwellers hear me as witnesses, how harsh words were spoken to me, who spoke what is right.
ramayana-3-43-28.meaning: He called the forest to witness.
ramayana-3-43-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-29.translation: Shame on you; may you perish, since you suspect me so, who stand by my elder's command, because of a woman's bad nature.
ramayana-3-43-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes. Lakshmana's generalisation about women reflects his anger and the attitudes of the time, not a teaching; the epic shows both him and Sita acting under great strain.

ramayana-3-43-30.translation: I will go where Rama is. May all be well with you, lovely one; may all the forest deities protect you, large-eyed one.
ramayana-3-43-30.meaning: He agreed to go, with a blessing.
ramayana-3-43-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-31.translation: For terrible omens are appearing to me; may I see you again with Rama when I return.'
ramayana-3-43-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-32.translation: Thus addressed by Lakshmana, Janaka's daughter, weeping, flooded with tears, replied sharply:
ramayana-3-43-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-33.translation: 'Without Rama, Lakshmana, I will enter the Godavari, or hang myself, or throw my body off a cliff,
ramayana-3-43-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-34.translation: or drink sharp poison, or enter fire; but I will never touch any man but Rama, even with my foot.'
ramayana-3-43-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-35.translation: Having cried out at Lakshmana, Sita, full of grief, weeping, struck her belly with her hands in sorrow.
ramayana-3-43-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-36.translation: Seeing her in distress, weeping, large-eyed, Lakshmana, troubled, tried to comfort her; but Sita said nothing to her husband's brother.
ramayana-3-43-36.meaning: She would not speak to him.
ramayana-3-43-36.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-43-37.translation: Then Lakshmana, with joined palms, bowed a little to Sita and, looking back at her many times, went toward Rama, self-controlled.
ramayana-3-43-37.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 43: hearing the cry, Sita begs Lakshmana to help Rama; when he refuses to leave her, she accuses him bitterly, and he goes.

ramayana-3-44-1.translation: Spoken to harshly by her and angry, Rama's younger brother, longing to see Rama, set out at once.
ramayana-3-44-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-2.translation: Ten-necked Ravana, seizing the opportunity, quickly came near Sita in the form of a wandering ascetic.
ramayana-3-44-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-3.translation: Wearing smooth ochre robes, with topknot, parasol and sandals, a staff and water pot hung on his left shoulder, in the guise of a wandering ascetic he approached Sita.
ramayana-3-44-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-4.translation: The very mighty one came upon her alone in the forest without the brothers, like great darkness upon twilight without sun and moon.
ramayana-3-44-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-5.translation: He saw the young, famous princess like Rohini without the moon, like a very dreadful planet.
ramayana-3-44-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-6.translation: Seeing that fierce evil-doer, the trees of Janasthana did not stir and the wind did not blow.
ramayana-3-44-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-7.translation: Seeing him look with red eyes, the swift-flowing Godavari began to flow sluggishly out of fear.
ramayana-3-44-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-8.translation: Seeking his chance in Rama's absence, Ravana approached Sita in the form of a mendicant.
ramayana-3-44-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-9.translation: The unworthy one in a worthy form approached Sita as she grieved for her husband, as Saturn approaches the star Chitra.
ramayana-3-44-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-10.translation: That sinner in a good form, like a well covered with grass, stood looking at Sita, Rama's famous wife,
ramayana-3-44-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest. The image of a grass-covered well warns how evil can hide behind a pleasing appearance.

ramayana-3-44-11.translation: lovely, with fine teeth and lips, face like the full moon, sitting in the leaf hut oppressed by tears and grief.
ramayana-3-44-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-12.translation: The wicked-minded night-roamer approached Sita, lotus-eyed, dressed in yellow silk.
ramayana-3-44-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-13.translation: Pierced by love's arrows, chanting Vedic recitation, the lord of demons spoke courteously to her in that lonely place.
ramayana-3-44-13.meaning: He spoke like a holy man.
ramayana-3-44-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-14.translation: Ravana praised her, the best in the three worlds, like Shri without her lotus, shining with her beauty.
ramayana-3-44-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-15.translation: 'Who are you, golden one in yellow silk, wearing a lovely lotus garland like a lotus pond?
ramayana-3-44-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-16.translation: Are you Modesty, Fortune, Fame, auspicious Lakshmi, or an apsara, lovely-faced one? Are you Prosperity, or Rati wandering at will?
ramayana-3-44-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-17.translation: Your teeth are even, pointed, glossy and white; your eyes are large and clear, red-cornered with dark pupils.
ramayana-3-44-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-18.translation: Your form is full and graceful.
ramayana-3-44-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest. Ravana's lustful praise here reveals his intent, not anything about Sita.

ramayana-3-44-19.translation: You are adorned with fine jewels and lovely.
ramayana-3-44-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-20.translation: Lovely-smiling, lovely-toothed, lovely-eyed, graceful lady, you steal my heart as a river's water steals its bank.
ramayana-3-44-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-21.translation: Slender-waisted, lovely-haired, neither goddess, gandharvi, yakshi nor kinnari
ramayana-3-44-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-22.translation: have I seen on earth such a woman before. Your living here in the wilderness unsettles my mind.
ramayana-3-44-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-23.translation: Turn back, bless you; you should not live here. This is the home of terrible shape-shifting demons.
ramayana-3-44-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-24.translation: Fine palaces, lovely city gardens, rich and fragrant, are fit for you to roam.
ramayana-3-44-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-25.translation: The best garland, the best drink, the best clothes, lovely one, and the best husband, I think, are fit for you, dark-eyed one.
ramayana-3-44-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-26.translation: Who are you, bright-smiling one, of the Rudras, Maruts or Vasus? You seem to me a goddess.
ramayana-3-44-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-27.translation: Neither gandharvas, gods nor kinnaras come here; this is the home of demons. How have you come here?
ramayana-3-44-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-28.translation: Here are monkeys, lions, leopards, tigers, bears, hyenas and herons; how are you not afraid of them?
ramayana-3-44-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-29.translation: How do you not fear, alone in the great forest, the terrible, strong, rutting elephants, lovely one?
ramayana-3-44-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-30.translation: Who are you, whose are you, where are you from, and why do you roam alone in the Dandaka, haunted by terrible demons, gracious one?'
ramayana-3-44-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-31.translation: Praised thus by wicked Ravana, Sita, seeing Ravana come in the dress of a brahmin, honoured him with all the courtesies due to a guest.
ramayana-3-44-31.meaning: Sita welcomed him as a guest.
ramayana-3-44-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-32.translation: First bringing a seat and inviting him with water for his feet, she said to the gentle-looking one, 'Food is ready.'
ramayana-3-44-32.meaning: She offered seat, water and food.
ramayana-3-44-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-33.translation: Seeing him come in a brahmin's dress with bowl and ochre cloth, Sita, seeing no way to refuse, invited him as one would a brahmin.
ramayana-3-44-33.meaning: She could not refuse a holy guest.
ramayana-3-44-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-34.translation: 'Here is a mat, brahmin, sit as you wish; take this water for your feet; and here is fine forest food prepared for you; enjoy it at ease.'
ramayana-3-44-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-35.translation: Invited by the king's wife, who spoke so courteously, Ravana looked at Sita, laughed, and set his mind on carrying her off, which would bring his own death.
ramayana-3-44-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-44-36.translation: Then, waiting for her well-dressed husband gone hunting, and for Lakshmana, she looked out and saw the great green forest, but not Rama and Lakshmana.
ramayana-3-44-36.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 44: Ravana, disguised as a wandering holy man, approaches Sita alone and praises her beauty; she welcomes him as a guest.

ramayana-3-45-1.translation: Questioned by Ravana in the form of a wandering ascetic, who wished to carry her off, Sita told him about herself.
ramayana-3-45-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana who she is.

ramayana-3-45-2.translation: 'He is a brahmin and a guest; if I do not answer he might curse me.' Thinking this for a moment, Sita spoke:
ramayana-3-45-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-3.translation: 'I am the daughter of the great Janaka of Mithila; my name is Sita, bless you, and I am Rama's wife, best of brahmins.
ramayana-3-45-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-4.translation: For a year I lived in Rama's home, enjoying human comforts and having all I wished.
ramayana-3-45-4.meaning: She told of her early married life.
ramayana-3-45-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-5.translation: After that year, my husband's father, with the royal ministers, decided to consecrate Rama as king.
ramayana-3-45-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-6.translation: While Rama's consecration was being prepared, a queen named Kaikeyi asked her husband for a boon.
ramayana-3-45-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-7.translation: Having bound my father-in-law by an earlier good deed, Kaikeyi asked the truthful best of kings for two things: my husband's exile and Bharata's consecration.
ramayana-3-45-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-8.translation: "I will not eat, sleep or drink ever again; this will be the end of my life if Rama is consecrated."
ramayana-3-45-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-9.translation: As Kaikeyi spoke, my father-in-law, giver of honour, begged her with fitting offers, but she would not grant his plea.
ramayana-3-45-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-10.translation: My husband, mighty, twenty-five years old, famed in the world as Rama, virtuous, truthful, pure, large-eyed, mighty-armed, devoted to the good of all beings,
ramayana-3-45-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-11.translation: came to his father for the consecration, and Kaikeyi quickly said to my husband:
ramayana-3-45-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-12.translation: "Hear from me, Rama, what your father has commanded: this kingdom must be given to Bharata without obstacle.
ramayana-3-45-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-13.translation: And you must live in the forest for fourteen years. Go into the forest, Rama, and free your father from untruth."
ramayana-3-45-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-14.translation: Rama, fearless, said 'So be it' to Kaikeyi, and my husband, firm in his vow, did as she said.
ramayana-3-45-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-15.translation: He would give but not take; he would speak truth and never falsehood: this, brahmin, is Rama's firm and supreme vow.
ramayana-3-45-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion. A beautiful summary of Rama's character.

ramayana-3-45-16.translation: His half-brother is the valiant Lakshmana, tiger among men, Rama's companion in battle and slayer of foes.
ramayana-3-45-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-17.translation: That brother named Lakshmana, following dharma and firm in his vow, followed him bow in hand as he went into exile with me.
ramayana-3-45-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-18.translation: So we three, cast out of the kingdom because of Kaikeyi, wander the deep forest by our own strength, best of brahmins.
ramayana-3-45-18.meaning: The three live in the forest.
ramayana-3-45-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-19.translation: Rest a moment; you can stay here. My husband will come bringing plenty of forest food.
ramayana-3-45-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-20.translation: Now tell me truly your name, your lineage and your family, and why you wander alone in the Dandaka forest, brahmin.'
ramayana-3-45-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-21.translation: As Sita, Rama's wife, spoke thus, mighty Ravana, lord of demons, gave a harsh reply:
ramayana-3-45-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-22.translation: 'I am he by whom the worlds, with gods, demons and serpents, are terrified: I am Ravana, Sita, lord of the hosts of demons.
ramayana-3-45-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-23.translation: Seeing you, golden-skinned, in silk, I no longer find delight in my own wives, faultless one.
ramayana-3-45-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-24.translation: Of the many fine women brought from here and there, be the chief queen of them all, bless you.
ramayana-3-45-24.meaning: He offered to make her queen.
ramayana-3-45-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-25.translation: My great city named Lanka is in the middle of the sea, surrounded by ocean and built on a mountain top.
ramayana-3-45-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-26.translation: There, Sita, you will roam its gardens with me, and you will not long for this forest life, lovely one.
ramayana-3-45-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-27.translation: Five thousand maidservants adorned with every ornament will serve you, Sita, if you become my wife.'
ramayana-3-45-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-28.translation: Thus addressed by Ravana, flawless Sita, angry, answered the demon with contempt:
ramayana-3-45-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-29.translation: 'I am devoted to Rama, unshakeable like a great mountain, like great Indra, imperturbable like the great ocean.
ramayana-3-45-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-30.translation: I am devoted to Rama, mighty-armed, broad-chested, walking with a lion's stride, a lion among men, like a lion.
ramayana-3-45-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-31.translation: I am devoted to Rama, moon-faced, heroic, beloved prince, master of his senses, of wide fame, mighty-armed.
ramayana-3-45-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-32.translation: And you, a jackal, want me, a lioness, hard to win. You cannot touch me, as one cannot touch the light of the sun.
ramayana-3-45-32.meaning: He is a jackal beside Rama.
ramayana-3-45-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-33.translation: Unlucky one, you must surely be seeing many golden trees, since you desire Rama's beloved wife, Ravana.
ramayana-3-45-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion. Seeing golden trees was believed to be a sign of approaching death.

ramayana-3-45-34.translation: You want to take a fang from the mouth of a hungry, swift lion, enemy of deer, or of a venomous snake.
ramayana-3-45-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-35.translation: You want to carry off Mandara, best of mountains, with your hand, or drink kalakuta poison and go away safe.
ramayana-3-45-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-36.translation: You rub your eye with a needle and lick a razor with your tongue, you who want to take Rama's beloved wife.
ramayana-3-45-36.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-37.translation: You want to cross the ocean with a stone tied round your neck, and seize both sun and moon with your hands, you who want to assault Rama's beloved wife.
ramayana-3-45-37.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-38.translation: Seeing a blazing fire, you want to carry it in a cloth, you who want to carry off Rama's virtuous wife.
ramayana-3-45-38.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-39.translation: You want to walk on the tips of iron spears, you who want to take a wife worthy of Rama.
ramayana-3-45-39.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-40.translation: The difference between a lion and a jackal in the forest, between a stream and the ocean, between fine wine and sour gruel: that is the difference between Rama and you.
ramayana-3-45-40.meaning: Rama and Ravana are worlds apart.
ramayana-3-45-40.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-41.translation: The difference between gold and lead, between sandal water and mud, between an elephant and a cat in the forest: that is the difference between Rama and you.
ramayana-3-45-41.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-42.translation: The difference between a crow and Garuda, between a cormorant and a peacock, between a crane and a vulture in the forest: that is the difference between Rama and you.
ramayana-3-45-42.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-43.translation: While Rama, equal in might to thousand-eyed Indra, stands with bow and arrows in hand, even if you carry me off you will not digest me, as a fly cannot digest a diamond it swallows.
ramayana-3-45-43.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-44.translation: Having spoken these well-considered words to the night-roamer, pure-hearted Sita trembled in body and was distressed, like a slender plantain shaken by wind.
ramayana-3-45-44.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-45-45.translation: Seeing Sita trembling, Ravana, like Death in power, told of his own family, strength, name and deeds to make her afraid.
ramayana-3-45-45.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 45: Sita tells the disguised Ravana her story; he reveals himself and asks her to be his queen, and she fiercely rejects him, comparing him to a jackal beside Rama the lion.

ramayana-3-46-1.translation: As Sita spoke thus, Ravana, enraged, knitting his brows, replied with harsh words:
ramayana-3-46-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-2.translation: 'I am the half-brother of Kubera, lovely one; I am Ravana, the mighty ten-necked one, bless you,
ramayana-3-46-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-3.translation: from whom gods, gandharvas, pishachas, birds and serpents flee in fear, as creatures always flee from death,
ramayana-3-46-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-4.translation: by whom my half-brother Kubera, for some cause, was challenged to a duel in anger and defeated in battle.
ramayana-3-46-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-5.translation: Afflicted by fear of me, Kubera left his rich capital and now lives on Kailasa, best of mountains.
ramayana-3-46-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-6.translation: His lovely wish-going chariot named Pushpaka I won by valour, lady, and in it I travel through the sky.
ramayana-3-46-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-7.translation: Seeing my face when I am angry, Sita, the gods led by Indra flee in terror.
ramayana-3-46-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-8.translation: Where I stand, the wind blows nervously, and the sun's fierce rays turn cool out of fear.
ramayana-3-46-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-9.translation: Wherever I stand or walk, the leaves of trees do not stir and the waters of rivers grow still.
ramayana-3-46-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-10.translation: Across the sea is my lovely city named Lanka, full of terrible demons, like Indra's Amaravati.
ramayana-3-46-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-11.translation: It is surrounded by a gleaming white wall, a lovely city with golden chambers and gateways of beryl,
ramayana-3-46-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-12.translation: crowded with elephants, horses and chariots, echoing with music, adorned with gardens full of trees that grant every wish.
ramayana-3-46-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-13.translation: Living there with me, princess Sita, proud one, you will not remember human women.
ramayana-3-46-13.meaning: You will forget your old life.
ramayana-3-46-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-14.translation: Enjoying human and divine pleasures, lovely one, you will not remember Rama, a mortal whose life is over.
ramayana-3-46-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-15.translation: He is the weak eldest son whom King Dasharatha sent away to the forest after installing his beloved son.
ramayana-3-46-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-16.translation: What will you do with that Rama, fallen from the kingdom, out of his mind, a wretched ascetic, large-eyed one?
ramayana-3-46-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-17.translation: You should not refuse the lord of all demons, who has come here himself out of desire, pierced by love's arrows.
ramayana-3-46-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-18.translation: For if you refuse me, timid one, you will suffer remorse, as Urvashi did after kicking Pururavas.'
ramayana-3-46-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-19.translation: Thus addressed, Sita, angry, her eyes red, spoke harsh words to the lord of demons in that lonely place:
ramayana-3-46-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-20.translation: 'How, naming as your brother the god Kubera, honoured by all beings, can you wish to do evil?
ramayana-3-46-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-21.translation: All the demons will surely perish, Ravana, whose king is you, harsh, foolish and without self-control.
ramayana-3-46-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-22.translation: One might carry off Indra's wife Shachi and live, but having carried me, Rama's wife, away there is no living.
ramayana-3-46-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-46-23.translation: One might live long after violating peerless Shachi from the hand of the thunderbolt-bearer, but having violated one like me, demon, there is no escape for you even if you have drunk nectar.'
ramayana-3-46-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 46: Ravana boasts of his power and Lanka's splendour; Sita warns that no one who takes Rama's wife can escape.

ramayana-3-47-1.translation: Hearing Sita's words, mighty ten-necked Ravana struck hand against hand and took on a huge form.
ramayana-3-47-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-2.translation: He spoke again forcefully to Sita: 'I think you are mad, not to have heard of my valour and might.
ramayana-3-47-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-3.translation: Standing in the sky I could lift the earth with my arms; I could drink the ocean and kill Death standing in battle.
ramayana-3-47-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-4.translation: I could block the sun with sharp arrows and split the earth. See me, mad one, who takes any form, a husband who grants every wish.'
ramayana-3-47-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-5.translation: As Ravana spoke thus in anger, his eyes, bright as flame, became red with tawny edges.
ramayana-3-47-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-6.translation: At once giving up the gentle mendicant form, Kubera's younger brother took his own form, like Death.
ramayana-3-47-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-7.translation: Red-eyed, glorious, with earrings of refined gold, ten-faced, with bow and arrows, the night-roamer appeared.
ramayana-3-47-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-8.translation: Throwing off the disguise of a wandering ascetic, the huge Ravana, lord of demons, took his own form.
ramayana-3-47-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-9.translation: Red-eyed with anger, dark as a mass of clouds, wearing red clothes, he stood looking at Sita, a jewel among women.
ramayana-3-47-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-10.translation: Ravana said to Sita, black-haired, like sunlight, with her clothes and ornaments:
ramayana-3-47-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-11.translation: 'If you want a husband famed in the three worlds, take refuge in me, lovely one; I am a husband fit for you.
ramayana-3-47-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-12.translation: Love me for ever; I am your praiseworthy beloved. I will never do anything to displease you, gracious one. Give up your feeling for a human and set your heart on me.
ramayana-3-47-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-13.translation: What virtues make you devoted to Rama, fallen from the kingdom, his aims unfulfilled, his life limited, foolish one who thinks herself wise?
ramayana-3-47-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-14.translation: The fool who at a woman's word left his kingdom and friends and lives in this forest haunted by beasts?'
ramayana-3-47-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-15.translation: Having said this to Sita, who deserved kindness and spoke kindly, Ravana seized her, like Budha seizing Rohini in the sky.
ramayana-3-47-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-16.translation: With his left hand he grabbed lotus-eyed Sita by her hair, and with his right he caught her by the legs.
ramayana-3-47-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana. The violent abduction is the turning point of the whole epic.

ramayana-3-47-17.translation: Seeing him like a mountain peak, sharp-fanged, mighty-armed, like Death, the forest deities fled in fear.
ramayana-3-47-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-18.translation: Then Ravana's great golden chariot, magical and divine, yoked to donkeys and with a harsh rattle, appeared.
ramayana-3-47-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-19.translation: Then, threatening her with harsh words, loud-voiced, he took Sita in his arms and put her in the chariot.
ramayana-3-47-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-20.translation: Seized by Ravana, the famous Sita, in anguish, cried out loudly 'Rama!' to Rama, who was far away in the forest.
ramayana-3-47-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-21.translation: Holding her, unwilling and writhing like a serpent king's wife, Ravana, tormented by desire, flew up.
ramayana-3-47-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-22.translation: Carried through the sky by the lord of demons, she cried out loudly, as if mad, distraught and in pain:
ramayana-3-47-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-23.translation: 'Ah Lakshmana, mighty-armed, who please your elder's heart, you do not know I am being carried off by a shape-shifting demon!
ramayana-3-47-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana takes his true form, seizes Sita and flies off in his chariot as she cries out for Rama and Lakshmana.

ramayana-3-47-24.translation: Rama, you who gave up life, happiness and wealth for dharma, do not see me being carried off unrighteously.
ramayana-3-47-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-25.translation: You are the punisher of the unruly, scorcher of foes; why do you not punish such an evil one as Ravana?
ramayana-3-47-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-26.translation: Surely the fruit of an unruly deed is seen at once; yet time too plays its part here, as in ripening crops.
ramayana-3-47-26.meaning: Wrongdoing will be repaid in time.
ramayana-3-47-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-27.translation: You have done this deed with your mind struck by fate; you will meet a terrible, life-ending disaster from Rama.
ramayana-3-47-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-28.translation: Now Kaikeyi and her kin have their wish, since I, the lawful wife of the famous lover of dharma, am being carried off.
ramayana-3-47-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-29.translation: I call on Janasthana and the flowering karnikara trees: tell Rama quickly that Ravana is carrying off Sita.
ramayana-3-47-29.meaning: Sita asked the trees to tell Rama.
ramayana-3-47-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-30.translation: I salute the peaked Malyavan and Mount Prasravana: tell Rama quickly that Ravana is carrying off Sita.
ramayana-3-47-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-31.translation: I salute the Godavari river, echoing with swans and cranes: tell Rama quickly that Ravana is carrying off Sita.
ramayana-3-47-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-32.translation: And to the deities who live in this forest of many trees I bow: tell my husband I have been carried off.
ramayana-3-47-32.meaning: She called on the forest spirits.
ramayana-3-47-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-33.translation: Whatever creatures live here, I take refuge in all of them, the herds of beasts and birds too.
ramayana-3-47-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-34.translation: Tell my husband that his beloved, dearer to him than life, has been carried off helpless by Ravana.
ramayana-3-47-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-35.translation: Knowing it, the mighty-armed, very strong one will bring me back by his valour, even from the other world, even if Yama himself had taken me.
ramayana-3-47-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-47-36.translation: Jatayu, you must tell Rama and Lakshmana exactly how I was carried off, all of it.'
ramayana-3-47-36.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 47: Ravana flies off with Sita, who cries out to Rama and asks the forest, river and creatures to tell Rama what has happened.

ramayana-3-48-1.translation: Jatayu, who had been sleeping, heard that cry; he quickly looked at Ravana and saw Sita.
ramayana-3-48-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-2.translation: Then the glorious best of birds, like a mountain peak, sharp-beaked, perched on a tree, spoke auspicious words:
ramayana-3-48-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-3.translation: 'Ten-necked one, I stand in ancient dharma and rely on truth; I am Jatayu, the mighty king of vultures.
ramayana-3-48-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-4.translation: Rama, son of Dasharatha, is king of the whole world, like great Indra and Varuna, devoted to the good of the worlds.
ramayana-3-48-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-5.translation: This is the lawful, famous wife of that lord of the world, lovely Sita, whom you want to carry off.
ramayana-3-48-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-6.translation: How can a king who stands in dharma touch another's wife? A king's wife above all must be protected, mighty one. Turn back your low intent of violating another's wife.
ramayana-3-48-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-7.translation: A wise man should not do what others would condemn in him; others' wives must be protected from violation just like one's own.
ramayana-3-48-7.meaning: Treat others' families as your own.
ramayana-3-48-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him. A clear statement of the golden rule.

ramayana-3-48-8.translation: In matters of wealth or pleasure not covered by the scriptures, the cultured follow the king's dharma, delight of the Paulastyas.
ramayana-3-48-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-9.translation: The king is dharma, desire and the best treasury of riches; dharma, good or evil, flows from the king.
ramayana-3-48-9.meaning: A ruler sets the moral tone.
ramayana-3-48-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-10.translation: How, being evil-natured and fickle, best of demons, have you gained power, like a sinner gaining a celestial chariot?
ramayana-3-48-10.meaning: Ravana does not deserve his power.
ramayana-3-48-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-11.translation: One's nature cannot be wiped away; and good fortune does not dwell long in the house of the wicked.
ramayana-3-48-11.meaning: Fortune does not stay with the wicked.
ramayana-3-48-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-12.translation: When righteous, mighty Rama does no wrong in your realm or city, how can you wrong him?
ramayana-3-48-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-13.translation: If Khara, who went to Janasthana because of Shurpanakha, overstepped and was killed by Rama, tireless in deeds,
ramayana-3-48-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-14.translation: tell me truly, what is Rama's offence, that you will go away having carried off the wife of the lord of the world?
ramayana-3-48-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-15.translation: Release Sita quickly, so that he does not burn you with his terrible fiery gaze, as Indra's thunderbolt burned Vritra.
ramayana-3-48-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-16.translation: You do not realise you have tied a venomous snake in the hem of your cloth, nor see the noose of Death around your neck.
ramayana-3-48-16.meaning: You are carrying your own death.
ramayana-3-48-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-17.translation: One should carry a load that does not crush one, gentle one, and eat food that digests without harm.
ramayana-3-48-17.meaning: Take on only what you can bear.
ramayana-3-48-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him. A practical teaching on knowing one's limits.

ramayana-3-48-18.translation: Who would do a deed that brings neither dharma, nor honour, nor fame on earth, but only weariness to the body?
ramayana-3-48-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-19.translation: Sixty thousand years have passed since I was born, Ravana, ruling properly my ancestral kingdom.
ramayana-3-48-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-20.translation: I am old, and you are young, an archer with chariot, armour and arrows; still, you will not go away safely taking Sita.
ramayana-3-48-20.meaning: Old as he is, he will fight.
ramayana-3-48-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-21.translation: You cannot carry Sita off by force while I watch, any more than one can overturn eternal Vedic truth with reasons.
ramayana-3-48-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-22.translation: Fight if you are brave; stand a moment, Ravana. You will lie slain on the ground, as Khara did before.
ramayana-3-48-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-23.translation: Rama in bark clothes, who has often killed daityas and danavas in battle, will soon kill you in battle.
ramayana-3-48-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-24.translation: What can I do, with the princes gone far away? You will soon perish, low one; you are afraid of them, no doubt.
ramayana-3-48-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-25.translation: While I live you will not take this lovely, lotus-eyed Sita, Rama's beloved queen.
ramayana-3-48-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-26.translation: I must do what pleases great Rama, and Dasharatha, even at the cost of my life.
ramayana-3-48-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-48-27.translation: Stop, stop, ten-necked one; wait a moment, Ravana. I will give you the hospitality of battle as far as my strength allows, night-roamer, and bring you down from your fine chariot like a fruit from its stalk.'
ramayana-3-48-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 48: the old vulture Jatayu wakes, warns Ravana that a king must not take another's wife, and challenges him.

ramayana-3-49-1.translation: Thus properly addressed by Jatayu, all twenty eyes of angry Ravana blazed like fire.
ramayana-3-49-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-2.translation: Red-eyed with rage, with earrings of refined gold, the impatient lord of demons rushed at the king of birds.
ramayana-3-49-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-3.translation: That tumultuous fight between the two in the great forest was like two clouds driven by wind in the sky.
ramayana-3-49-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-4.translation: That fight between the vulture and the demon was wondrous, like two great winged mountains with garlands.
ramayana-3-49-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-5.translation: Then the mighty one showered the king of vultures with very dreadful tubular, iron, sharp-pointed and barbed arrows.
ramayana-3-49-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-6.translation: Jatayu, lord of birds, received those nets of arrows, Ravana's weapons, in battle.
ramayana-3-49-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-7.translation: With his feet and sharp claws the mighty best of birds made many wounds on Ravana's body.
ramayana-3-49-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-8.translation: Then in anger ten-necked Ravana took ten terrible arrows like Death's rod, wanting to crush his enemy.
ramayana-3-49-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-9.translation: The mighty one pierced the vulture with those sharp, terrible, straight-flying arrows shot at full draw.
ramayana-3-49-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-10.translation: Seeing Sita in the demon's chariot with tearful eyes, he ignored those arrows and rushed at the demon.
ramayana-3-49-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-11.translation: Then the mighty lord of birds broke with his feet Ravana's bow, with its arrow, adorned with pearls and gems.
ramayana-3-49-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-12.translation: And with his wings the mighty lord of birds shook off Ravana's blazing, fire-like armour.
ramayana-3-49-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-13.translation: The strong one killed in battle his swift goblin-faced donkeys with their golden breastplates.
ramayana-3-49-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-14.translation: He broke the great chariot, with its triple pole, wish-going, fire-bright, patterned with gems and gold, and the parasol like the full moon, with the fans.
ramayana-3-49-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-15.translation: With his bow broken, chariotless, his donkeys and charioteer killed, Ravana fell to the ground holding Sita in his arms.
ramayana-3-49-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-16.translation: Seeing Ravana fallen to the ground, his vehicle broken, all beings honoured the king of vultures, crying 'Well done!'
ramayana-3-49-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-17.translation: But seeing the leader of birds exhausted by old age, Ravana, delighted, rose up again holding Sita.
ramayana-3-49-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-18.translation: As he went off joyfully with Sita on his lap, Jatayu, king of vultures, flew up and said:
ramayana-3-49-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-19.translation: 'Foolish Ravana, you are carrying off the wife of Rama, whose arrows strike like thunderbolts, surely for the death of the demons.
ramayana-3-49-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-20.translation: With friends, kin, ministers, army and attendants, you are drinking this poison like a thirsty man drinks water.
ramayana-3-49-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-21.translation: The unwise, who do not know the consequences of their deeds, quickly perish, as you will perish.
ramayana-3-49-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings. A teaching on thinking before acting.

ramayana-3-49-22.translation: You are bound by the noose of Time; where can you go to escape it? Like a fish taking a baited hook to its death.
ramayana-3-49-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-23.translation: The two invincible Raghus will never forgive you this violation of their hermitage, Ravana.
ramayana-3-49-23.meaning: Rama and Lakshmana will avenge this.
ramayana-3-49-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-24.translation: The deed you have done, coward, is condemned by the world; this is the way of thieves, not of heroes.
ramayana-3-49-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-25.translation: Fight if you are brave; stand a moment, Ravana. You will lie slain on the ground like your brother Khara.
ramayana-3-49-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-26.translation: A man at the time of his death takes up an unrighteous deed; you have taken up this deed for your own ruin.
ramayana-3-49-26.meaning: This is a deed of doom.
ramayana-3-49-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-27.translation: What man would do a deed bound up with sin, even if he were lord of the world or the self-born Brahma himself?'
ramayana-3-49-27.meaning: No one should do such a thing.
ramayana-3-49-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-28.translation: Having spoken these good words, the valiant Jatayu fell hard upon ten-necked Ravana's back.
ramayana-3-49-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-29.translation: Seizing him, he tore at him all over with sharp claws, like an elephant rider mounting a wild elephant.
ramayana-3-49-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-30.translation: He tore with his claws, struck his beak into his back and pulled out his hair, using claws, wings and beak as weapons.
ramayana-3-49-30.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-31.translation: Tormented again and again by the king of vultures, the demon trembled, his lips quivering with rage.
ramayana-3-49-31.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-32.translation: Holding Sita with his left side, Ravana, in pain and faint with anger, struck Jatayu with his palm.
ramayana-3-49-32.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-33.translation: Jatayu, the lord of birds, subduer of foes, evaded him and tore off his ten left arms with his beak.
ramayana-3-49-33.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-34.translation: Then angry ten-necked Ravana let Sita go and pounded the king of vultures with fists and feet.
ramayana-3-49-34.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-35.translation: Then for a moment there was a battle between the two of matchless might, the chief of demons and the best of birds.
ramayana-3-49-35.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-36.translation: As he struggled for Rama's sake, Ravana drew his sword and cut off his wings, feet and sides.
ramayana-3-49-36.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-37.translation: His wings cut off suddenly by the demon of cruel deeds, the vulture fell to the ground, struck down, with little life left.
ramayana-3-49-37.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-38.translation: Seeing Jatayu fallen on the ground wet with blood, Sita ran to him in grief, as to her own kin.
ramayana-3-49-38.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-39.translation: The lord of Lanka saw Jatayu on the earth, like a blue-black cloud, with a white chest, of noble valour, like a forest fire put out.
ramayana-3-49-39.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-49-40.translation: Then moon-faced Sita, daughter of Janaka, embraced the bird felled to the ground, crushed by Ravana's force, and wept.
ramayana-3-49-40.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 49: Jatayu fights Ravana, destroys his chariot and bow, but is finally struck down when Ravana cuts off his wings.

ramayana-3-50-1.translation: The lord of demons saw the vulture fallen on the ground near Rama's hermitage, quivering, with little life left.
ramayana-3-50-1.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-2.translation: Moon-faced Sita, seeing the king of vultures slain by Ravana, lamented in great sorrow:
ramayana-3-50-2.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-3.translation: 'Omens, knowledge of signs, and seeing and hearing birds surely show men their joys and sorrows.
ramayana-3-50-3.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-4.translation: Surely, Rama, you do not know of this great disaster; surely beasts and birds are running to you for my sake.
ramayana-3-50-4.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-5.translation: Save me today, Rama! Lakshmana!' the noble lady cried, terrified, as if they could hear her close by.
ramayana-3-50-5.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-6.translation: As she lamented as if helpless, her garlands and ornaments crushed, Ravana, lord of demons, rushed at Sita.
ramayana-3-50-6.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-7.translation: As she clung like a creeper, embracing great trees, the lord of demons said again and again, 'Let go, let go!'
ramayana-3-50-7.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-8.translation: As she cried 'Rama, Rama!' without Rama in the forest, he, like Death, seized her by the hair, to his own life's end.
ramayana-3-50-8.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-9.translation: When Sita was violated, the whole world, moving and unmoving, went beyond its bounds and was covered in blind darkness.
ramayana-3-50-9.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves.

ramayana-3-50-10.translation: Seeing Sita seized and wretched, glorious Brahma, the Grandfather, said with divine sight, 'The purpose is accomplished.'
ramayana-3-50-10.meaning: Brahma saw this would lead to Ravana's end.
ramayana-3-50-10.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana seizes Sita again as she clings to the trees, and all creation grieves. The abduction sets in motion the defeat of Ravana for which Rama was born.

ramayana-3-50-11.translation: All the great seers living in the Dandaka forest, seeing Sita seized, were both glad and grieved.
ramayana-3-50-11.meaning: The sages saw both sorrow and the coming end of evil.
ramayana-3-50-11.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-12.translation: Ravana, lord of demons, went into the sky carrying her as she wept, 'Rama, Rama!' and 'Lakshmana!'
ramayana-3-50-12.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-13.translation: Every limb adorned with gold, wearing yellow silk, the princess shone like a flash of lightning.
ramayana-3-50-13.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-14.translation: With her yellow garment fluttering, Ravana shone all the more, like a mountain lit by fire.
ramayana-3-50-14.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-15.translation: Fragrant coppery lotus petals from the most gracious Sita scattered over Ravana.
ramayana-3-50-15.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-16.translation: Her silk, fluttering in the sky with a golden glow, looked like a copper cloud lit by the sun.
ramayana-3-50-16.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-17.translation: Her clear face in Ravana's lap in the sky did not shine without Rama, like a lotus without its stalk.
ramayana-3-50-17.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-18.translation: It was like the moon risen after splitting a dark cloud: lovely forehead and hairline, like the heart of a lotus, flawless, adorned with bright white teeth,
ramayana-3-50-18.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-19.translation: weeping, tears wiped away, lovely as the moon, with fine nose and lovely red lips, shining like gold in the sky.
ramayana-3-50-19.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-20.translation: Her lovely face, shaken by the demon king, did not shine without Rama, like the moon risen by day.
ramayana-3-50-20.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-21.translation: Golden Sita against the dark-limbed demon king shone like a golden girdle around a sapphire.
ramayana-3-50-21.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-22.translation: Fair as a lotus, golden, with burning ornaments, Sita shone against Ravana like lightning entering a cloud.
ramayana-3-50-22.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-23.translation: With the jingle of Sita's ornaments, the demon king looked like a dark, clear cloud with thunder.
ramayana-3-50-23.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-24.translation: A shower of flowers fell from her head all around to the ground as Sita was carried off.
ramayana-3-50-24.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-25.translation: Shaken by Ravana's speed, that shower of flowers swirled back around the ten-necked one.
ramayana-3-50-25.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-26.translation: The stream of flowers circled Kubera's younger brother like a clear garland of stars around Mount Meru.
ramayana-3-50-26.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-27.translation: Her jewelled anklet slipped from her foot and fell with a sweet sound, like a ring of lightning.
ramayana-3-50-27.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-28.translation: Red as a young shoot, Sita adorned the dark demon king like a golden girth on an elephant.
ramayana-3-50-28.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.

ramayana-3-50-29.translation: Kubera's younger brother carried Sita into the sky, blazing with her own radiance like a great meteor.
ramayana-3-50-29.explanation: Aranya Kanda, chapter 50: Ravana carries Sita through the sky; her ornaments and flowers fall, and all of nature grieves.
